reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / WHO / India NTEP
clinicalPearls: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis is defined by resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, the two most important first-line drugs
Rifampicin resistance detected on rapid molecular testing is treated as a marker for probable MDR-TB and triggers a drug-resistant TB treatment pathway
Resistance may be primary, from transmission of a resistant strain, or acquired through inadequate, interrupted or poorly supervised prior treatment
Further resistance to fluoroquinolones and other key agents defines pre-XDR and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis, which are harder to treat
Rapid molecular tests such as cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification and line-probe assays allow early detection of resistance and should be used up front
Modern treatment favours all-oral, shorter, drug-susceptibility-guided regimens including newer agents such as bedaquiline and linezolid, delivered under programmatic support
India's NTEP provides free universal drug-susceptibility testing and standardised drug-resistant TB regimens, with active follow-up to improve adherence and outcomes
reference.pathophysiology: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis arises from spontaneous chromosomal mutations in genes encoding drug targets or activating enzymes, for example rpoB mutations conferring rifampicin resistance and katG or inhA mutations conferring isoniazid resistance. Selective pressure from inadequate drug exposure, poor adherence, or malabsorption allows resistant mutants to become the dominant population. Sequential accumulation of mutations produces multidrug and extensively drug-resistant strains. These resistant organisms can be transmitted directly to new hosts, so resistance is propagated both by acquisition during treatment and by primary transmission within communities.
additionalDifferentials: Drug-susceptible tuberculosis with treatment failure from non-adherence
Malabsorption of anti-tuberculosis drugs mimicking resistance
Paradoxical reaction or immune reconstitution rather than true failure
infectionMimics: Drug-susceptible TB failing due to poor adherence
Post-tuberculous lung damage with secondary infection
additionalInvestigations: Rapid molecular testing (cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification) for rifampicin resistance at diagnosis
Line-probe assays and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing to define the resistance pattern
Baseline and monitoring investigations for drug toxicity (audiometry, ECG for QT, liver and renal function)
HIV testing and screening of close contacts
redFlags: Rifampicin resistance on molecular testing requiring urgent switch to a drug-resistant TB pathway
Extensive or progressive disease with respiratory compromise
Emergence of additional resistance (pre-XDR or XDR) narrowing treatment options
Public health emergency of transmission of resistant strains, especially in congregate or HIV settings
reference.prognosis: Outcomes have improved substantially with all-oral shorter regimens containing newer agents, but MDR-TB still carries higher treatment failure, relapse and mortality than drug-susceptible disease, with worse outcomes as resistance broadens or when treatment is delayed.
pitfalls: Adding a single new drug to a failing regimen, which amplifies resistance
Delaying drug-susceptibility testing and treating empirically as drug-susceptible disease
Under-recognising drug toxicities such as QT prolongation and peripheral neuropathy during monitoring
Neglecting adherence support and contact tracing, allowing transmission
